evidence: Abstract: 'On Granite, our method improves accuracy by approximately 2.3 percentage points on average over a parameter-matched routing baseline... Our code is available in the supplementary materials.'

Table 1 (Section 4.2): TES-IS improves ARC-Challenge over Dual Affinity by 1.07 points on Granite and 2.26 on OLMoE; OLMoE frozen-affinity CE (63.27 ARC, 70.40 OpenBookQA) outperforms ACS-IS (62.73, 69.93), showing task- and backbone-dependent gains.

Section 4.1 and Appendix A.7: fixed 500-example test sets, custom deterministic partitions, answer-text scoring protocol; 'examples from an official test partition can therefore occur in the custom training partition. These results should not be interpreted as official-test evaluations.'

Appendix A.5: transformation ablation 'combines transformation and initialization effects and should not be interpreted as a fully isolated causal estimate'; started-log improves group Pearson from 0.398 to 0.452 but pure-log has 0.40 pt higher accuracy.
Section 3.5: TES adds N(d+1) parameters and O(Nd) operations per supervised MoE layer while preserving native top-K budget; ACS adds no parameters.

Section 5 Limitations: 'Our evaluation covers two sparse MoE backbones, four multiple-choice question-answering benchmarks... Larger-scale models and pretraining-scale optimization are outside the scope of this evaluation'; no end-to-end latency/memory measurement.

Appendix A.9/A.12: ACS diagnostics show mean concentration rises from ~0.26 to ~0.78-0.81, but 'these shifts... are descriptive and do not establish that increased concentration causes the corresponding accuracy differences.'
llm_evaluation.rationale: A methods paper on sparse MoE routing for LLMs, squarely within high-weight preferences (LLMs, MoE/Transformer architecture, training/optimization) and not a capped out-of-scope domain. Novelty is moderate: directly supervising routers with realized token loss via a head-based (TES) and headless (ACS) mechanism using IS/ENLL objectives is a fresh but incremental angle that the paper itself traces to MoGU, learned-loss prediction, and difficulty-based routing lines. Rigor is solid: parameter-matched controls (Dual Affinity), gradient/optimum analysis in appendices, coefficient/depth/transformation ablations, and honest reporting of negative and confounded results. Evidence strength is tempered by 500-example custom test splits (explicitly 'should not be interpreted as official-test evaluations', Appendix A.7), only 3 seeds, modest 0.5-3 pt gains, mixed OLMoE outcomes (frozen-affinity CE beats ACS on ARC/OpenBookQA), and a transformation ablation the authors concede confounds initialization. Generalizability is limited to LoRA-adapted 1-3B MoE backbones and MCQA; pretraining scale is acknowledged out of scope. Reproducibility is good: full config tables, seeds, split construction, prompts, and a code-availability claim in supplementary materials.

Section 4.1 Implementation Details: 6K synthetic QA pairs for MMSI-Bench and 10K for VSI-Bench; baselines fine-tuned on other spatial datasets with identical hyperparameters
Table 5 (Section 4.4): agent topology ablation shows QA generation success 34.0% (1 agent) vs 92.0% (4 agents) on 100 seeds; Qwen3.5-9B generator drops to 48.0%
Table 6 (Section 4.5): direct Gemini3.5-Flash annotation yields 28.2 avg vs 42.9 for Exemplar2VQA on VSI-Bench MC subset

llm_evaluation.rationale: Core methodology is an LLM multi-agent coding pipeline (Qwen3-Coder-30B agents with Architect/Coder/Reviewer/Refiner roles and a geometric tool API) for synthetic spatial VQA data, followed by SFT/LoRA of Qwen2.5-VL models - strongly matching Agents & Tool Use, Code & Programming, LLMs, Reasoning, and Multimodal AI preferences, though it lacks any Japanese NLP content and the domain is spatial VQA rather than pure language modeling. Novelty is moderate: deterministic code-execution for spatial reasoning and multi-agent decomposition build on cited prior work (Code as Policies, ViperGPT, PAL, CLEVR-style rule-based generation); the exemplar-to-template abstraction and simulator-feedback refinement are incremental combinations. Rigor is reasonably solid (topology and generator-capacity ablations, direct-LLM-annotation comparison, matched-hyperparameter baselines, seed-stability table, error analysis, limitations section) but weakened by suspicious generator model names (Qwen3.5-9B, Gemini3.5-Flash), VSI-Bench evaluation restricted to the multiple-choice subset in the main table, small 100-seed ablations, and admitted absence of error bars for headline results. Generalizability is a strength (indoor-to-outdoor transfer, four+ benchmarks, backbone transfer). links.title: Pretraining Latent Information Feedback Transformers with Teacher Supervision

evidence: Abstract: 'Experiments with pretrained models ranging from 135M to 1B parameters show that LIFT consistently outperforms standard Transformers and baselines on language modeling, downstream reasoning tasks, and procedural tasks under token-matched budget.'

§5.2 / Table 1: 'At matched tokens, LIFT is ahead on every metric at every scale: perplexity drops by 5–5.5%, and it wins 33 of the 36 downstream benchmark comparisons'; compute-matched Transformers train on >40% more tokens yet LIFT 'keeps the lead on every metric at 350M and 1B'.

§4 Results: two-layer LIFT solves 12-step S5 sequences at 100% accuracy 'even when the states come from a Transformer teacher that itself fails at that length (3%)', extrapolating to 96% at N=32 and 65% at N=64; §C.1 shows Transformer gains saturate by 20× budget.

§D.1: 'At 135M, LIFT improves perplexity over the compute-matched Transformer by 0.47±0.08'; the no-teacher self-state variant ties it (+0.01±0.05), so 'the teacher thus accounts for 98% of LIFT's gain', and input-only (λ=0) falls behind—supporting the mechanism claims with controls.

Appendix B.2–B.4: complete configs (OLMo 2 codebase/data, WSD schedule, k=1024, τ=1.5, λ=1.5, data mix percentages); footnote 1 releases code and trained models at https://github.com/dortirosh1/LIFT/.

§C.4 Table 10 and Table 14 give three-seed mean±sd; §7 acknowledges teacher-architecture/vocabulary limits and the unexplored beyond-teacher-budget regime; §F.1 notes the compute-matched accounting inadvertently favored baselines by ~2.5% more tokens.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core LLM methodology paper: modifies Transformer pretraining to add a teacher-forced latent feedback channel, directly matching the highest-weight preferences (LLMs, Transformer architecture, reasoning, training/scaling). Not a domain application; clearly in scope. Novelty is solid but incremental over a dense related-work field (Coconut, T2MLR, PonderLM, CoCoMix, Thinking States); the specific combination—teacher-forced next-token distributions as pretraining inputs with self-state adaptation—is credibly claimed as first (Table 20). Rigor is high: token- and compute-matched baselines, distillation and channel-off controls isolating the mechanism, ablations over teacher use, channel width k, trunk vs. adaptation phase, and teacher strength, three seeds at 135M plus seed tables, paired bootstrap intervals, and FLOPs/memory accounting. Evidence is strong at small scale; the 350M/1B results rest on single seeds and several matched-compute downstream gaps are honestly reported as within noise. Generalizability is good across 135M–1B and two setups but bounded by shared-tokenizer teachers and OLMo 2/SmolLM2 backbones; limitations are acknowledged (§7). Reproducibility is strong: code and models released, exhaustive hyperparameters in Appendices A–B. Aggregate ≈0.86.

primary_link.title: Pretraining Latent Information Feedback Transformers with Teacher Supervision

top5.summary: Transformer language models (LMs) are feed-forward: deep-layer representations are never fed back to shallower layers, and the only pathway for information to flow downward across generation steps is the decoded token. This narrow channel forces models to recompute intermediate results and to discard alternative continuations. In this work, we remove this bottleneck during pretraining, introducing the LIFT (Latent Information Feedback Transformer) architecture and training method which enable LM
top5.summary_zh: Transformer 語言模型屬前饋架構，深層表徵無法回饋至淺層，跨步驟傳遞資訊僅能依賴單一解碼 token（約17位元），迫使模型重複計算中間結果並捨棄其他可能的延續。本文提出 LIFT（Latent Information Feedback Transformer），將遞迴狀態學習轉為 teacher-forced 預測問題：凍結的預訓練「教師」模型以平行前向運算，在每個位置產生下一 token 分布並截取 top-k 作為狀態，與輸入 token 配對；學生模型經輕量融合層同時預測下一 token 與下一狀態，並以 KL 對齊項監督，使訓練完全保持平行。最後10%訓練改用自身狀態並搭配 prefix state dropout，以支援平行 prefill。實驗顯示，兩層 LIFT 在 S5 狀態追蹤任務可解12步序列（100%準確率），即使教師本身僅3%；135M至1B參數預訓練指出，在相同 token 與計算量預算下，LIFT 困惑度下降約5%，於36項下游比較中贏得33項，算術與模式延續等程序性任務增益最大，且優於 Jacobi 疊代回饋基線。限制在於教師與學生共享架構與詞彙表、推論時狀態須逐步回饋，以及訓練遠超教師預算時的行為仍待探究。此研究證明語言模型能在預訓練階段以可擴展的教師監督習得深層至淺層回饋，兼具遞迴式表達能力與平行訓練效率。
top5.title: Pretraining Latent Information Feedback Transformers with Teacher Supervision
top5.title_zh: 以教師監督預訓練潛在資訊回饋 Transformer

links.title: LeapQuant: Efficient Linear Attention with Accurate Recurrent State Quantization

evidence: Abstract & Section 4.2: 'With 8-bit quantization, LeapQuant achieves accuracy on par with the FP32 baseline across the 12 model–task pairs'; Table 1 shows Ours 8-bit avg 75.5 equal to FP32 75.5 while BF16 per-step drops Qwen3.5-9B AIME to 72.1.
Section 4.4 Table 2: staged ablation raises INT8 AIME from 7.1 (per-step) to 82.4 (+per-window), 86.6 (+Compensator Tokens), 87.9 (+smoothing) at 2.52x kernel speedup.

Section 4.3: kernel speedups of 2.68x/3.95x/4.25x (GDN) and 2.41x/3.38x/3.64x (KDA) at batch 512; state stored at 1.19 bytes/element vs 4 (3.4x traffic reduction); end-to-end memory cut 41-56% with prefix caching.

Section 4.1: baselines span FP8/INT8/MXFP/NVFP4/MXFP4 plus adapted KVQuant, QuaRot, TurboQuant; 'Due to limited hardware resources, we run only 8-layer versions of Qwen3.8-Flash and GLM-5.3-Flash ... use them only for efficiency measurements.'
Appendix A Table 4: the general update form covers Linear Attention, RetNet, Mamba2, GLA/RWKV6/HGRN2, DeltaNet, Gated DeltaNet, KDA, RWKV7, DeltaProduct, supporting architectural generalizability.
Section 4.1 states implementation in vLLM with TileLang kernels and Table 6 lists full sampling parameters, but no code or artifact availability claim appears anywhere in the paper.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core LLM-inference efficiency paper: training-free quantization of the recurrent state in linear-attention hybrid LLMs (GDN/KDA), directly matching the LLM, transformer-architecture/SSM, scaling-efficiency, and inference-serving preferences. Novelty is solid rather than groundbreaking: per-window quantization exploits the known chunkwise unrolling of linear attention, and Compensator Tokens are a rank-one outlier-absorption scheme in the spirit of SVDQuant/GEAR, though the reuse of the delta-rule update path and the error-accumulation analysis (Appendix B.1) are new for recurrent states. Rigor is strong: 5 models, 5 benchmarks, 8/6/4-bit comparisons against FP8/INT8/MXFP/KVQuant/QuaRot/TurboQuant (Appendix C), three-seed averaging, staged ablations (Table 2), and p/r sweeps (Table 3); deducted for no variance reporting and for baselines that must be adapted rather than purpose-built, plus 8-layer proxy models for two efficiency-only evaluations (Section 4.1). Evidence is internally consistent (Table 1 avg 75.5 matches FP32; ablation endpoints match Table 1), though speedup figures cannot be verified from text. Generalizes across the recurrence family (Appendix A Table 4) and is calibration-free, but is specific to delta-rule-style linear attention states. No explicit code/artifact release is stated, lowering reproducibility despite detailed hyperparameters (p=16, r=4) and Table 6 sampling settings.

primary_link.title: LeapQuant: Efficient Linear Attention with Accurate Recurrent State Quantization

top5.summary: Recent LLMs increasingly adopt hybrid designs that replace standard attention with linear attention, such as Gated DeltaNet (GDN) and Kimi Delta Attention (KDA). Although they compress the context into a fixed-size recurrent state and substantially reduce the cost of long-context processing, repeatedly reading and updating that state remains a major inference bottleneck. Quantization offers a natural way to reduce this cost, but can significantly degrade model quality, due to the accumulation of
top5.summary_zh: 本文針對線性注意力（如 Gated DeltaNet 與 KDA）推論時的遞迴狀態存取瓶頸提出解方。此類混合架構將上下文壓縮成固定大小的遞迴狀態，但解碼每個 token 都需在 HBM 讀寫整個狀態，頻寬與記憶體成本高昂；直接量化狀態雖可省成本，但逐步重量化會累積捨入誤差，加上狀態少數行列藏有極大離群值，使低精度儲存後品質崩壞。LeapQuant 為免訓練方法，提出兩項技術：其一為 per-window quantization，每 16 個 token 的窗口僅在邊界量化狀態一次，窗口內以高精度緩衝更新計算輸出，降低誤差累積頻率；其二為 Compensator Tokens，以少數高精度秩一（rank-one）項保留狀態的最大離群結構，沿用真實 token 的更新路徑，再對殘差做跨通道平滑後量化。在 Qwen3.5、Kimi-Linear 與 GLM 模型家族上，8-bit 量化之下游準確率與 FP32 基準相當（平均 75.5%），6-bit 達 72.4%，4-bit 仍達 60.4%，遠優於 FP8、INT8、KVQuant 等基準；狀態記憶體流量降低 3.4 倍，端對端記憶體最多省 56%，於 B200、RTX PRO 6000 與 RTX 5090 上核心層級加速 2.05–3.70 倍、端對端加速 1.47 倍。限制：方法針對對角衰減加 delta rule 的遞迴形式設計，補償 token 過多（如 r=16）會使核心反而慢於 FP32，部分效率量測採用刪減層數的模型。整體而言，本方法讓低精度遞迴狀態在長推理與長上下文混合模型的服務中成為可行預設，極具實務部署價值。

links.title: EngiWorld: What Can Frontier Agents Deliver in Professional Engineering Environments?

evidence: Abstract: '1,301 expert-curated tasks spanning 6 engineering domains (CAD, CAE, CAM, BIM, EDA, and 3D visualization) and 26 professional software platforms'; 'the strongest model achieves an EngiScore of only 44.3, and just 3.6% of multi-software attempts succeed.'

Section 3.4 / Section 4.1: artifact-centric evaluation with equations (1)-(3); evaluation of seven models on 'the same stratified subset of 300 tasks, comprising 152 CLI-interface tasks and 148 GUI-interface tasks' in a zero-shot setting.

Appendix B.3, Table B.3: verifier validation — all 96 reference artifacts accepted, 40+40 alternative-solver and 5 alternative-design submissions accepted, 21 empty and 21 metrics-only submissions all rejected; text notes 'tolerance-boundary tests are outside the completed audit populations.'

Section 4.3, Tables 3-4 and Figure 6: ablations on initial-image presentation (GPT GUI 15.0→31.7 with message placement), runtime image access (readimg helps Gemini, hurts Kimi), accessibility trees, resolution, and history length, with model-dependent effects explicitly acknowledged.

Section 4.4, Table D.1: failure taxonomy over 3,347 distinct failed runs — DONE with zero score 49.03%, decision-turn limit 44.79%; Table D.3 lists four verified violations in agent-declared successes (e.g., GPT-5.6 Sol left 3.698 mm3 residual material vs 0.1 mm3 allowance).

Appendix C.3, Table C.3: paired Multi-software vs Open-ended analysis — all seven models fail the Multi-software versions of tasks 02/09, while four models succeed on Open-ended task 09, isolating delivery/handoff failures from geometric capability.

Reproducibility: Appendix B.1 Table B.1 lists 37 environments with software versions and OS; Section 4.1 specifies PyAutoGUI, 1920×1080 screenshots, 15-round history, and step limits; a project page URL is given but no explicit code/task-release commitment appears in the text.
llm_evaluation.rationale: A large-scale agent benchmark evaluating seven frontier LLM/MLLM agents on professional engineering software via GUI/CLI interaction, squarely matching Agents & Tool Use and LLM preferences plus evaluation methodology. Novelty is moderate: it unifies existing ideas (OSWorld-style interaction, single-domain artifact verifiers) into a 6-domain/26-platform suite with a continuous quantitative-design score, but the methodology components are largely assembled from prior work. Rigor is solid — formal task/scoring formulation, verifier validation with reference, alternative-valid, and defective populations (Table B.3), stratified 300-task main evaluation, ablations, and a failure taxonomy — though it lacks statistical treatment, single-run evaluations, small strata (only 4 Open-ended tasks in the main eval), and an admittedly incomplete verifier audit ('tolerance-boundary tests are outside the completed audit populations'). Evidence is extensive and internally consistent (per-category scores, token/cost accounting, verified violation case studies), but no explicit code/data release statement appears beyond a project-page URL, limiting reproducibility despite detailed environment/version documentation. Findings are honestly framed as model-dependent, which caps generalizability claims.

primary_link.title: EngiWorld: What Can Frontier Agents Deliver in Professional Engineering Environments?

top5.summary: Autonomous agents have made rapid progress in general-purpose computer use, but reliable automation of professional industrial engineering remains out of reach, as engineering workflows demand reasoning over geometric and physical constraints and dependencies preserved across software and design stages. We present EngiWorld, the first benchmark structured around the complete design loop: 1,301 expert-curated tasks spanning 6 engineering domains (CAD, CAE, CAM, BIM, EDA, and 3D visualization) and
top5.summary_zh: 「EngiWorld」是首個以完整設計迴圈為架構的基準測試，旨在評估 AI 代理於專業工程軟體環境中的表現。研究指出，現有電腦使用基準（如 OSWorld、Spider2-V）多僅比對最終狀態，無法驗證工程成品的幾何有效性、物理可行性與規範合規性，且互動深度不足、缺乏領域原生回饋。為此，作者邀集領域專家，透過 LLM 輔助流程建立 1,301 道任務，涵蓋 CAD、CAE、CAM、BIM、EDA 與 3D 視覺化六大領域、26 套軟體平台，提供 GUI 與命令列兩種介面，以及影像建模、軟體選擇、單軟體長程執行、量化設計、多軟體協作與開放式任務六類題型。評估採「以成品為中心」的方法，以統一的領域驗證器程式化檢查最終與中間產出，量化設計任務依規格達成度給予連續分數而非二元判定。實驗在 300 道分層抽樣任務上評測七個前沿模型：Claude Opus 5 以 EngiScore 44.3 居首，GPT-5.6 Sol 為 38.0，但多軟體任務成功率僅約 3.6%，且 300 題中有 128 題所有模型皆得零分。失敗分析顯示「未通過驗證即宣告完成」與決策輪次耗盡合占 94.1%，消融實驗也顯示觀測設計的效益因模型而異。限制在於主評測僅取樣部分任務以控制成本，驗證器容差邊界測試尚未全面完成，且 CAM 領域對所有模型最為困難。整體而言，本基準揭示了通用工具操作與可靠工程執行之間的根本落差，可作為發展工業級代理的嚴謹基礎。

§3 Propositions 1–4 and Corollary 1: GRPO update is uniform in ψ=arcsin√p up to boundary ramps; zero-variance probability bounded by Gaussian layers e^{-Gψ²}+e^{-G(π/2−ψ)²}; evidence variance 1/(4n); pass@k gradients are Gaussians with mode arcsin(1/√(2k)); any fixed sampler w(ψ) ascends a derived objective F_w.
§5.3 Table 3: ablations quantify components — Gaussian over raw p −0.69, logit-space Kalman −0.96, no dead-zone factor ŷ −1.03, fixed pass@1 target −0.62, reward-feedback pacing −0.85.

Appendix B.10 Table 4: exact numerical verification of all analytic claims (e.g., Prop.1 matches Davis & Recht weight to <10⁻¹⁴; TV between H_k and Laplace kernel 0.050–0.069), produced by code/theory_checks.py.

§5.5 and Appendix F Tables 11–12, 15: gains persist on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B (+2.4 vs GRPO), Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct (+1.9), MATH pool (+2.2), and under Dr. GRPO/DAPO/RLOO losses (+1.1–1.2 over DS).
Appendix D/E Tables 5–6 plus reproducibility checklist (i)–(vi): full hyperparameters, algorithm pseudocode, seeded Gumbel noise, three training seeds; no external code-release URL stated.
Limitations section: derived for binary rewards and std-dev-normalized GRPO; experiments cover mathematical reasoning, models ≤7B, G≤16; code and agentic tasks remain untested.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core LLM methodology paper: improves GRPO (RLVR) post-training for mathematical reasoning by deriving a Fisher–Rao arc-length coordinate for pass rates and building Arcus, a closed-form Kalman-filter prompt sampler with objective pacing. Strongly matches high-weight preferences (LLMs, reasoning, RL, training/efficiency). Novelty is solid but derivative in part: the arcsine objective of GRPO is credited to Davis & Recht (2025), and Anscombe/variance-stabilization, Kalman filtering, and Gumbel-top-k are classical; the contribution is composing them into a geometry-derived sampler that provably reshapes the implicit objective (Corollary 1) and predicts waste (Prop. 7). Rigor is high: four propositions with proofs (App. B), exact numerical checks (App. B.10, Table 4), extensive ablations isolating coordinate/kernel/pacing (Tables 3, 8), mechanism analysis, three seeds with s.d. (Table 7). Evidence is strong: best averages on all three backbones (Table 1), 48–57% fewer rollouts than DS, cost and wall-clock breakdowns (Tables 2, 6), generality across backbones, pools, and losses (Tables 11, 12, 15). Generalizability is limited by math-only binary-reward evaluation, models ≤7B, G≤16 (Limitations), though the theory formally extends to any binary verifier. Reproducibility is good (full hyperparameters, Algorithms 1–2, evaluation protocol, reproducibility checklist), but no external code-release URL is verifiable, only internal script references. Minor caution: evaluation sets like AIME (30 problems) are small, mitigated by multi-seed and multi-benchmark averaging.

primary_link.title: Prompts Live on an Arc: Gaussian Curricula in Fisher--Rao Coordinates for Rollout-Efficient GRPO

top5.summary: Group relative policy optimization (GRPO) learns only from prompts whose sampled responses disagree: a group that is entirely correct or entirely incorrect has zero reward variance, contributes no gradient, and still consumes its rollouts. Prompt-selection methods reduce this waste by steering sampling toward intermediate pass rates, but they choose the target, its width, and the uncertainty model heuristically, in raw pass-rate or logit coordinates. We show that GRPO comes with a natural coordi
top5.summary_zh: 此論文探討 GRPO(群組相對策略最佳化)在可驗證獎勵強化學習(RLVR)中的取樣浪費:當同一提示詞的一組回覆全對或全錯(零變異數)時,優勢歸零、不產生梯度,卻已付出 rollout 成本。作者指出 GRPO 天然具有 Fisher–Rao 幾何:以弧長 ψ=arcsin√p 為座標時,期望更新近乎均勻、零變異機率形成兩端高斯邊界層、答對率證據的雜訊為常數 1/(4n),而 pass@k 與 pass^k 目標的梯度皆為封閉形式的高斯核。據此提出 Arcus:為每個提示詞在弧長座標上維護卡爾曼濾波器信念,以與目標匹配的高斯核乘上資訊性群組機率來評分,僅讓資訊性群組進入未更動的 GRPO 更新,並以節奏規則將目標推向預測產出仍與最佳值相差小於 ε 的最難目標。實驗在三個骨幹模型與六個數學推理基準(含 AIME24/25、AMC23、MATH500 等)顯示,Arcus 較 GRPO 平均提升 2.8–2.9 個百分點、較動態取樣(DS)提升 1.1–1.2 個百分點,同時比 DS 少生成 48–57% 的 rollout,並以少 70% 的 rollout 達到 DS 的最終準確率;消融實驗顯示座標選擇貢獻最大。限制包括:理論僅適用於二元獎勵與 GRPO 的標準差正規化,Dr. GRPO 等變體的原生座標不同,連續獎勵需另行轉換;實驗限於數學推理,模型至多 7B、群組大小 ≤16,程式碼與代理任務尚未驗證。此研究的意義在於證明取樣器本身即決定 GRPO 上升的目標函數,可在不改動損失的前提下兼顧準確率與運算成本。

llm_evaluation.rationale: Highly relevant: an LLM-safety/mechanistic-interpretability study localizing prompt-injection compliance via causal activation patching across five open models (Qwen3-4B/14B/32B, Phi-3-mini, Mistral-7B), with detection, probing, and agentic/robustness follow-ups. Novelty is solid but incremental over refusal-direction and intermediate-layer detection work (Arditi et al. 2024; Wen et al. 2025), which it explicitly positions against. Rigor is strong: control batteries (benign/compliant/norm-matched random), same-prompt analyses, sublayer decomposition, rank-k PCA, split-half subspace validation, temperature/GCG/multi-turn robustness, and public-benchmark replication with benchmark-matched donors; honest negative results (agentic single-token patching fails, MoE weak, naturalistic flip ~12%) are reported. Evidence is detailed and appropriately hedged, though the headline 77-92% figure comes from a synthetic single-turn AcmeCorp setting and labels rely on keyword matching plus an LLM judge. Generalizability is partial: the clean early-decode/late-cause dissociation holds mainly for dense non-thinking models, English-only stimuli, and peak layers vary (63-91% depth). Reproducibility is moderate: public models, system prompts, and benchmark datasets are specified, but the synthetic corpus and code are not explicitly released.

primary_link.title: Where Do LLMs Decide to Break the Rules? Mechanistic Localization of Prompt Injection Compliance

top5.summary: When a prompt injection attack succeeds, a Large Language Model (LLM) abandons its assigned system role to comply with an adversarial instruction. While prior work has extensively quantified how often this occurs, we ask a more fundamental question: where inside the network does the model actually decide to break the rules? Using layer-by-layer causal activation patching across five models (4B to 32B parameters), we find a clear dissociation: attack information is linearly decodable from the fir
top5.summary_zh: 當提示注入攻擊得手,LLM 會拋棄系統角色聽從惡意指令。過去研究多量化攻擊成功率,本文追問:模型在網路內部哪一層「決定」違規?作者以逐層因果活化修補為核心,在五個 4B 至 32B 參數模型上攔截前向傳遞,將隱藏狀態替換為抵抗樣本平均狀態,並測量翻轉率。結果呈現明確分離:攻擊資訊自第一層即可線性解碼(各層探針準確率逾八成),但對行為的因果槓桿在網路前半段近乎為零,直到最後三分之一才出現晚期瓶頸;修補該瓶頸可讓 77% 至 92% 的服從案例翻轉為拒絕。此機制佔據低維線性子空間(4B、14B 約 rank-8,32B 為 rank-64),跨架構、解碼溫度、GCG 對抗後綴與多輪情境皆穩定位於晚層;潛行攻擊雖走不同的早期表徵路徑,最終仍匯聚於同一瓶頸。偵測實驗亦印證機制:因果峰值層 L24 為最佳偵測位置(AUROC 0.993),在 leetspeak 等五種混淆下召回率 100%,遠優於第一層分類器(13.3%)。限制:峰值層須逐模型標定(佔深度 63%–91%);實驗多為英文、單輪合成情境;自然基準翻轉率降至約 12%,間接注入依賴乾淨捐贈者;推理、MoE 與代理場景中單 token 介入明顯減弱。整體而言,本文將「知道」與「行動」在網路深度上分離,指出監控與介入應聚焦於因果槓桿集中的晚層,為可解釋的安全防禦與輕量偵測提供結構性依據。
